hypotheses.weekly: Change only rebalance cadence to first VN trading session of each ISO week; compare monthly. More buys may be cost-only churn.
hypotheses.slope90: Weekly rank using (exp(252 * OLS slope of log close on time over 90 sessions)-1) * R-squared. Same 254-bar eligibility, sizing and buffer as control. Clenow-inspired ranking only, not full book replication.
hypotheses.quality: Weekly: first top20 12-1 momentum, then rank by negative information discreteness: -sign(12-1 return)*(fraction negative minus fraction positive daily returns over formation). Ties use 12-1 then symbol. Keep top20 hold buffer and inverse-vol sizing. Gray/Vogel-inspired two-stage adaptation to 30 names, not their published strategy.
hypotheses.breakout50: Weekly control targets, but each attempted purchase requires prior completed close > max high of preceding 50 sessions (excluding signal bar). Apply to new and add-on buys. A channel-breakout proxy, not CAN SLIM or chart-pattern replication.
hypotheses.breakout50_volume: Same breakout gate plus signal-bar volume >=1.5 * preceding 50-session average volume. Compare breakout without volume to isolate incremental signal. O'Neil/IBD-inspired price-volume proxy only. No historical earnings availability, no claim to full CAN SLIM.

invariants: All 10 parent windows, PIT membership, prior-close inputs, next-open execution, fees, T+3 settlement, no leverage.
180 portfolio trials = 10 windows x 6 variants x 3 execution/cost scenarios. No parameter grid search, combined winners, or threshold retuning after results.
Weekly membership and gates are rechecked before every retry. Delay stress may use newly completed entry evidence, but quantities remain from scheduled decision.
Frequency counts separate filled buys, flat-to-long entries, additions, unique buy dates and rebalances. Broker fill count is not independent trade count.
Paired tests on continuous normal-case returns only; family 27 includes 22 previous registered comparisons plus 5 new comparisons. Historical global trial count remains unknown.
